persons.name: Śaṅkarasiṃha
persons.evidence: śāntaḥ śaṅkarasiṃha ity avitathaṃ nāmāpi ramyaṃ vahan

persons.name: Lakṣmaṇasiṃha
persons.evidence: tasyāpatyam ... śrīmān lakṣmaṇasiṃha ... śāstraṃ śrīharivaṃse (!) saṃjñakam idaṃ sa śraddhapālālikhat

notes: The date is expressed by the chronogram nayana-graha-kara = 292 (NS 292 = c. 1172 CE). The phrase 'sa śraddhapālālikhat' is metrically (Śārdūlavikrīḍita: – – ◡ – – ◡ –) and contextually a scribal error or misreading for 'sa śraddhayālīlikhat' ('he caused [the book] to be written with devotion/faith'); therefore Lakṣmaṇasiṃha is the commissioner and there is no scribe named Śraddhapāla. The royal name Caruṭadeva is unusual and unattested elsewhere; it may be a misreading or variant for Rudradeva (II), who was reigning in Nepal around NS 287–296.
